notes:
BATCH U (inhalers): budesonide/formoterol, fluticasone propionate/salmeterol, fluticasone propionate/formoterol, tiotropium, fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol, salbutamol (pMDI + nebuliser solution), salbutamol/budesonide.
NO UK PRODUCT: salbutamol/budesonide (clinic trade name and ingredient pair searched on emc; MHRA Products search index has no product with both substances) -> availability no-uk-product, no rules.
STRENGTH NOTES: budesonide/formoterol uses the UK 200/6 metered (160/4.5 delivered) dry powder inhaler SmPC, matching the clinic dose. Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol: one UK SmPC covers 50/100, 50/250 and 50/500 dry powder inhaler; the clinic 50/250 is NOT the COPD strength (only 50/500) and is not for children under 12 (only 50/100 from 4 years); age rule coded 'dose'. Fluticasone propionate/formoterol: emc 7649 (125/5) and 7648 (250/10) have identical SmPC text (diffed); each formulation cites its own page. Fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol UK SmPC (03 Jun 2025) is COPD-only and says it should not be used in asthma (coded avoid).
CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules): (1) Pregnancy: fluticasone propionate/formoterol SmPC 'not recommended' (avoid) and tiotropium SmPC 'preferable to avoid' (avoid) vs BUMPS (inhaled corticosteroids should be continued; asthma medicines' benefits usually outweigh risks; tiotropium named as a LAMA). Salbutamol inhaler SmPC 'should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary' (avoid) vs nebuliser SmPC 'only if benefit outweighs risk' (caution) vs BUMPS (no harm shown, continue). (2) Breastfeeding: SmPCs 'decide whether to stop breastfeeding or therapy' / tiotropium 'not recommended' vs SPS (inhaled budesonide and fluticasone can be used; SPS does not cover formoterol, salmeterol, vilanterol, umeclidinium or tiotropium; no SPS page found for salbutamol). (3) Nebuliser specialist wording: SmPC says 'specialists in respiratory medicine', MHRA DSU says 'specialists in asthma'. (4) QT: formoterol SmPCs list QTc caution and QT-drug interactions; SPS QT page (Aug 2026) says beta-2 agonist inhalers alone pose low QT risk and a low likelihood of clinically significant interaction with other QT-prolonging medicines. For this reason NO inhaler was added to group qt-prolonging (that would fire every macrolide/quinolone/SSRI QT rule); SmPC QT interaction rules are kept on the inhaler side only.
LEVEL DECISIONS FOR REVIEW: (a) Salbutamol 'asthma' condition rule is 'avoid' with concern 'SABA prescribed WITHOUT an inhaled corticosteroid' (MHRA 2025 'do not prescribe SABA ... without a concomitant prescription of an inhaled corticosteroid', NICE NG245 1.6.3). The engine cannot test for absence of an ICS, so it will show for every asthma patient on salbutamol; the concern text states the condition. Same pattern for tiotropium 'should not be used as monotherapy for asthma' (avoid). (b) Salbutamol 4.3 'non-IV formulations must not be used to arrest uncomplicated premature labour or threatened abortion' is a pregnancy rule 'contraindicated' (fires for any pregnancy; concern names the tocolysis use). (c) Seretide-type and Symbicort-type lactose (milk protein) excipient: 4.3 hypersensitivity to excipients + 6.1 'lactose (which contains milk proteins)' coded contraindicated for condition cows-milk-protein-allergy; the triple inhaler 6.1 lists lactose without a milk-protein statement, so only the galactose-intolerance 'should not use' rule. (d) Fluticasone/salmeterol and fluticasone/formoterol 'CYP3A inhibitors' statements cover potent AND moderate inhibitors, so they use group:cyp3a4-inhibitor; budesonide/formoterol names clarithromycin explicitly (rule other: clarithromycin); the triple inhaler names strong inhibitors only (group:strong-cyp3a4-inhibitor).
LABA WITHOUT ICS (MHRA DSU Sept 2010): 'always prescribe LABA with concomitant ICS and only when ICS alone are not sufficient'; recorded in restrictions for the three ICS/LABA products (all already contain an ICS, so no engine rule). MHRA DSU April 2025 + NICE NG245 SABA-without-ICS recorded for salbutamol (restrictions + rule).
BRAND / DEVICE PRESCRIBING: SPS 'Example medicines to prescribe by brand name' (2 Apr 2026): 'tiotropium capsules, cartridges and administration devices should be prescribed by brand name' (tiotropium brandPrescribing); same page: 'Generic prescribing of inhalers can lead to people being given an unfamiliar device'. SPS 'Prescribing by generic or brand name' lists 'dry powder inhalers' as a device example where brand prescribing is necessary -> brandPrescribing set for the three dry powder inhalers (budesonide/formoterol, fluticasone/salmeterol, triple). For the pressurised inhalers (fluticasone/formoterol pMDI, salbutamol pMDI) no UK source says to prescribe by brand: brandPrescribing null, the general SPS sentence is in restrictions (detail). NICE NG245 1.6.8 'same type of device for preventer and reliever' recorded. No MHRA brand-prescribing statement found for these inhalers (MHRA brand advice exists for beclometasone pMDIs, not in this batch).
GROUPS: new groups long-acting-beta2-agonist and long-acting-muscarinic-antagonist (used by the triple inhaler 'other LAMA/LABA not recommended' rules). Inhaled products were deliberately NOT added to 'corticosteroid' (systemic steroid group used by NSAID GI-bleeding and hypokalaemia rules) nor to 'sympathomimetic' (batch T xylometazoline contraindicates 'other sympathomimetic decongestants' and amitriptyline avoids sympathomimetics such as adrenaline; inhaled salbutamol/vilanterol membership would mis-fire those). Tiotropium 'other anticholinergic' rule uses group:anticholinergic; amitriptyline (batch P) is a member, so it will fire; ipratropium membership must come from batch V (tiotropium also has an explicit allergy rule for ipratropium from its 4.3). Hypokalaemia rules use group:diuretic where the SmPC says 'diuretics' (that group includes spironolactone) and group:thiazide/group:loop-diuretic where it says non-potassium-sparing; loop-diuretic and thiazide membership relies on other batches.
CONDITIONS reused from other batches: cardiac-arrhythmia and urinary-retention (batch P), hocm (O), phaeochromocytoma (M/T), prostatic-hypertrophy, acute-asthma-attack, renal-impairment (A), galactose-intolerance-lactase-deficiency (B), cardiac-disease (F). 'Idiopathic subvalvular aortic stenosis' is mapped to hocm (same rule concern text).
NOT FOUND / NOT USED: no SPS breastfeeding page for salbutamol, LABAs or LAMAs; no BUMPS leaflets for formoterol, salmeterol or tiotropium (404; BUMPS asthma and inhaled-corticosteroid leaflets used). Renal/hepatic not stated for salbutamol. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). Salbutamol inhaler SmPC 4.8 frequency text is jumbled in the page text, so frequencies are quoted from the nebuliser SmPC (same list).
AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker, see audit/T-U.md): no-uk-product for salbutamol/budesonide confirmed with the MHRA products search index (no SPC/PIL with both substances). salbutamol-budesonide added to beta2-agonist and inhaled-corticosteroid (ingredient-level UK SmPC quotes), the same approach batch T uses for its no-uk-product combinations, so that other medicines' group rules still reach it. Newer MHRA products SPC texts were compared with the emc texts used: Symbicort 200/6 (07/06/2023), Seretide 50/250 (17/11/2023), Spiriva Respimat (14/01/2025) and Ventolin Respirator (23/01/2024) have no clinically relevant differences in 4.1-4.6, except that the newer 50/250 Seretide text states the COPD indication without naming the 50/500 strength (posology still 50/500 only). QT: SPS lists beta-2 agonists (salbutamol, formoterol) on its QT page but says the risk with inhalers alone is low and a clinically significant interaction with other QT drugs is unlikely; inhalers stay out of qt-prolonging (integrator to confirm against the QT group policy).
CROSS-BATCH GROUP AUDIT 2026-10-17 (audit/groups-cross-batch.md, sources/XB.json): superseded two decisions above. (a) 'sympathomimetic' is now the broad group and includes salbutamol and the three LABA-containing inhalers (UK quotes in XB.json); the xylometazoline contraindication and the amitriptyline 'not recommended' rule were retargeted to the new 'decongestant' group, so inhalers no longer reach them. (b) tiotropium, ipratropium and the triple inhaler moved from 'anticholinergic' to the new 'inhaled-antimuscarinic' group; tiotropium, ipratropium and hyoscine butylbromide have companion rules for the inhaled group. Flutiform's 'other adrenergic drugs' caution now excepts salbutamol (same SmPC: inhaled SABA for relief between doses; separate info rule).
